prior.title: Signed numbers
prior.reminder: Use a number line: adding moves right; subtracting moves left.

steps.prompt: Calculate −3 + 8.
steps.hint: Start at −3 and move 8 places right.

steps.prompt: Calculate 4 − 9.

prior.title: Order of operations
prior.reminder: Brackets first, then powers, then multiplication/division, then addition/subtraction.

steps.prompt: Calculate 3 + 4 × 2.
Calculate (3 + 4) × 2.
steps.hint: This time the brackets come first.

prior.title: Fractions and decimals
prior.reminder: A fraction means division. For example, 1/2 = 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5.

steps.prompt: Write 3/4 as a decimal.
Calculate 1/2 + 1/4. Give a decimal.

prior.title: Percentages
prior.reminder: Percent means out of 100. For example, 10% of 80 is 0.10 × 80 = 8.

steps.prompt: Find 10% of 60.
A price of 60 increases by 10%. Find the new price.
steps.hint: Add the increase to the original price.

prior.title: Ratios and proportion
prior.reminder: For a ratio of 2:3, there are 5 equal parts altogether.

steps.prompt: Share 20 in the ratio 2:3. What is the size of one part?
What is the larger share?

prior.title: Powers and roots
prior.reminder: 3² means 3 × 3. A square root reverses squaring for a non-negative number.

steps.prompt: Calculate 3².
Calculate √49.

prior.title: Substitution
prior.reminder: Replace a letter by its value. In 2x + 1 with x = 3, calculate 2 × 3 + 1 = 7.

steps.prompt: Evaluate 3x + 2 when x = 4.
Evaluate x² + 2 when x = −3.

prior.title: Undoing operations
prior.reminder: Keep both sides equal: use the same operation on each side.

steps.prompt: Solve x + 5 = 12. Enter x.
Solve 3x = 12. Enter x.

prior.title: Converting units
prior.reminder: 1 m = 100 cm; 1 hour = 60 minutes. Use the unit to choose the conversion.

steps.prompt: Convert 2.5 m to cm.
Convert 90 minutes to hours.
For the point (−2, 5), enter its y-coordinate.
A graph rises from y = 3 to y = 9. Find the change in y.

prior.title: Area and right triangles
prior.reminder: Rectangle area = length × width. For a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.

steps.prompt: Find the area of a rectangle 4 cm by 3 cm, in cm².
A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. Find its hypotenuse.

prior.title: Calculator confidence
prior.reminder: Enter brackets carefully. Keep extra digits until the final answer; check that the size of the result makes sense.

steps.prompt: Evaluate (6 + 4) ÷ 2.
steps.hint: Enter the brackets, then divide the whole sum by 2.

steps.prompt: Round 7.386 to two decimal places.
steps.hint: Look at the third decimal digit, 6.

sections.title: Write a number in standard form
sections.reminder: Standard form separates a number into a coefficient and a power of ten.

steps.prompt: Calculate 10³.
Calculate 4 × 10³.

sections.title: Continue an arithmetic sequence
sections.reminder: An arithmetic sequence adds the same amount each time.

steps.prompt: For 3, 7, 11, … find the common difference.
steps.hint: Subtract one term from the next.

steps.prompt: Find the next term after 11.

sections.title: Continue a geometric sequence
sections.reminder: A geometric sequence multiplies by the same amount each time.

steps.prompt: For 2, 6, 18, … find the common ratio.
steps.hint: Divide one term by the previous term.

steps.prompt: Find the next term after 18.

sections.title: One year of growth
sections.reminder: A 5% increase means multiplying by 1.05.

steps.prompt: Find 5% of 200.
Find the balance after 200 earns 5% for one year.
steps.hint: Add the interest to the initial amount.

sections.title: Read a logarithm
sections.reminder: log₁₀(100) asks: what power of 10 gives 100?

steps.prompt: Calculate 10².
Find log₁₀(100).

sections.title: Round and find a bound
sections.reminder: A measurement rounded to the nearest whole unit can be half a unit away.

steps.prompt: Round 6.37 to one decimal place.
A length rounds to 8 cm to the nearest cm. Find its lower bound.

sections.title: One loan payment
sections.reminder: Apply the period’s interest first, then subtract the payment.

steps.prompt: A debt of 100 earns 2% interest this month. Find the interest.
You then pay 20. Find the remaining debt.

sections.title: Solve two equations
sections.reminder: Use an equation to replace an unknown in the other equation.

steps.prompt: Given x + y = 7 and x = 3, find y.
For this x and y, calculate 2x + y.

sections.title: Find a slope
sections.reminder: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.

steps.prompt: Between (1, 3) and (3, 7), find the change in y.
steps.hint: Subtract the first y-value from the second.

steps.prompt: Find the slope between these points.
steps.hint: Divide the change in y by 3 − 1.

sections.title: Use a function machine
sections.reminder: f(x) is the output when the input is x; it does not mean f multiplied by x.

steps.prompt: If f(x) = 2x + 1, find f(3).
For the same function, which input gives output 9?

sections.title: Add two functions
sections.reminder: To add functions at an input, calculate both outputs and then add them.

steps.prompt: If f(x) = x², find f(2).
If g(x) = x + 1, find f(2) + g(2).

sections.title: Find an intercept
sections.reminder: At a y-intercept, x = 0. At an x-intercept, y = 0.

steps.prompt: For y = 2x − 6, find y when x = 0.
For y = 2x − 6, find x when y = 0.

sections.title: Use a simple cost model
sections.reminder: A fixed starting cost becomes the constant; a cost per item becomes the multiplier.

steps.prompt: A trip costs 4 plus 2 per km. Find the cost for 3 km.
How much extra does one more km cost?
steps.hint: Look at the cost per km.

sections.title: Check a prediction
sections.reminder: Residual = observed value − predicted value. A model is a useful approximation.

steps.prompt: A model y = 2x + 1 predicts a value at x = 4. Find the prediction.
The observed value is 10. Find the residual.

sections.title: Build a cuboid
sections.reminder: Cuboid volume = length × width × height. Volume has cubic units.

steps.prompt: A cuboid base is 3 cm by 4 cm. Find its base area in cm².
The height is 2 cm. Find the volume in cm³.
steps.hint: Multiply the base area by the height.

sections.title: Use a trigonometric ratio
sections.reminder: sin(angle) = opposite ÷ hypotenuse. Check that your calculator is in degrees.

steps.prompt: A right triangle has opposite side 3 and hypotenuse 6. Find sin(angle).
Use inverse sine in degree mode to find the angle.

sections.title: Read a bearing
sections.reminder: Bearings are measured clockwise from north: north 000°, east 090°, south 180°, west 270°.

steps.prompt: Enter the bearing of east as a number.
You travel east, then turn directly back. Enter the return bearing.

sections.title: Take a fraction of a circle
sections.reminder: A sector with angle 90° is 90/360 of a full circle.

steps.prompt: What fraction of a circle is 90°? Give a decimal.
A circle has circumference 20 cm. Find the 90° arc length in cm.

sections.title: Find a midpoint and bisector
sections.reminder: A midpoint is halfway between two points. A perpendicular bisector passes through it at a right angle.

steps.prompt: Find the midpoint x-coordinate between (2, 0) and (8, 0).
Their perpendicular bisector has equation x = k. Find k.
steps.hint: The segment is horizontal, so its bisector is vertical through the midpoint.

sections.title: Find the nearer site
sections.reminder: A Voronoi region contains points nearer its site than any other site.

steps.prompt: A is at (0, 0), B at (10, 0). Find the distance from (3, 0) to A.
steps.hint: All points lie on the same horizontal line.

steps.prompt: Find the distance from (3, 0) to B.
steps.hint: Subtract 3 from 10; compare the two distances.
steps.working: 10 − 3 = 7. Since 3 < 7, the point is in A’s region.

sections.title: Population and sample
sections.reminder: The population is the whole group of interest; the sample is the smaller group measured.

steps.prompt: A school has 200 students and surveys 20. What is the sample size?
What percentage of the population is sampled?

sections.title: Add frequencies
sections.reminder: Frequency is the number of observations in a group. Cumulative frequency is a running total.

steps.prompt: Groups A, B and C have frequencies 3, 5 and 2. Find the total.
Find the cumulative frequency up to and including group B.

sections.title: Find mean and median
sections.reminder: Mean = sum ÷ number of values. Median = middle value after sorting.

steps.prompt: Find the mean of 2, 4 and 9.
steps.hint: Add the values, then divide by 3.

steps.prompt: Find the median of 2, 4 and 9.
steps.hint: The list is already sorted; take the middle.

sections.title: Predict from a line
sections.reminder: A regression line predicts y from x. A prediction need not equal an actual observation.

steps.prompt: For the fitted line y = 3x + 2, predict y at x = 2.
Predict y at x = 3.
steps.hint: Use the same line with the new input.

sections.title: Probability from counts
sections.reminder: For equally likely outcomes: probability = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.

steps.prompt: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue counters. How many counters are there?
Find the probability of drawing red. Give a decimal.
steps.hint: Divide the red count by the total.

sections.title: Probability without replacement
sections.reminder: Without replacement means the first item is not returned; update both counts.

steps.prompt: A bag starts with 3 red and 2 blue. A red is removed. How many red remain?
Now find the probability the next counter is red. Give a decimal.
steps.hint: There are 4 counters left, including 2 red.

sections.title: Expected value
sections.reminder: Expected value is the sum of each outcome multiplied by its probability.

steps.prompt: A game pays 10 with probability 0.2 and 0 otherwise. Find 10 × 0.2.
steps.hint: Multiply the prize by its chance.

steps.prompt: Find the expected prize.
steps.hint: Add the contribution from a zero prize, which is 0.

sections.title: Binomial mean
sections.reminder: For n independent trials with constant success probability p, the expected number of successes is np.

steps.prompt: There are 10 trials and p = 0.3. Find the expected successes.
If there are 20 trials with the same p, find the expected successes.

sections.title: Standardize a value
sections.reminder: A z-score counts standard deviations from the mean: z = (x − mean) ÷ SD.

steps.prompt: A distribution has mean 50 and SD 10. How far above the mean is 60?
Find the z-score of 60.
steps.hint: Divide the difference by the SD, 10.

sections.title: Rank observations
sections.reminder: Assign rank 1 to the smallest value. Tied values share the average of their positions.

steps.prompt: In the data 10, 20, 30, what is the rank of 20?
In 10, 20, 20, 30, what rank should each 20 receive?

sections.title: Read a significance threshold
sections.reminder: Compare the p-value with α in the same units. Reject H₀ when p ≤ α.

steps.prompt: Write a 5% significance level as a decimal.
The p-value is 0.03. How far below 0.05 is it?
steps.hint: Calculate 0.05 − 0.03, then decide whether to reject H₀.

sections.title: Average rate of change
sections.reminder: Average rate = change in output ÷ change in input. A derivative is a limiting rate.

steps.prompt: Distance changes from 4 m to 10 m. Find the change in metres.
The change took 2 seconds. Find the average rate in m/s.
steps.hint: Divide distance change by time change.

sections.title: Read a derivative’s sign
sections.reminder: A positive derivative means locally increasing; a negative one means locally decreasing.

steps.prompt: For f′(x) = 2x, calculate f′(3).
steps.working: 2 × 3 = 6, so the function is increasing there.

steps.prompt: Calculate f′(−2).
steps.working: 2 × (−2) = −4, so the function is decreasing there.

sections.title: Use the power rule
sections.reminder: The derivative of axⁿ is (a × n)xⁿ⁻¹: multiply the coefficient by n and reduce the power by 1.

steps.prompt: For f(x) = 3x², find the coefficient of x in f′(x).
steps.hint: Multiply the coefficient 3 by the power 2.

steps.prompt: Find f′(2).

sections.title: Find a tangent slope
sections.reminder: The derivative at a point is the slope of the tangent there.

steps.prompt: For y = x², the derivative is 2x. Find the tangent slope at x = 1.
Find the normal slope at the same point.
steps.hint: For a nonzero tangent slope m, use −1/m.

sections.title: Area under a constant graph
sections.reminder: A definite integral of a positive function gives the area between its graph and the x-axis.

steps.prompt: Under y = 3 from x = 0 to x = 4, find the width of the rectangle.
steps.hint: Subtract the lower x-bound from the upper.

steps.prompt: Find the area, which is the integral over this interval.

sections.title: Locate a stationary point
sections.reminder: At a stationary point the derivative is zero. Its sign on either side tells you more.

steps.prompt: If f′(x) = 2x − 4, solve f′(x) = 0. Enter x.
Evaluate the derivative at x = 3, to the right of the stationary point.
steps.working: 6 − 4 = 2. At x = 1 it is −2, so the sign changes from negative to positive: a minimum.

sections.title: Compare possible areas
sections.reminder: Optimization means choosing the best allowed value, such as the largest area.

steps.prompt: A rectangle with perimeter 20 has width 2 and length 8. Find its area.
A square with the same perimeter has sides 5. Find its area.
steps.working: Area = 25. Comparing examples suggests a better shape; a full optimization justifies the maximum.

sections.title: One trapezoid
sections.reminder: Trapezoid area = width × (first height + second height) ÷ 2.

steps.prompt: A strip has end heights 2 and 6. Find their average.
steps.hint: Add the heights and divide by 2.

steps.prompt: The strip width is 3. Find the trapezoid area.
steps.hint: Multiply the width by the average height.
